resources.string: Bubble Keyboard is your current keyboard
How see-through the bubble is while it rests; it turns solid when you open it
How far keys grow and slide out from under your finger in a bloom
How long the open ring waits untouched before folding up. The arc around the center counts it down; it pauses while you dictate.
Turns the punctuation and number fans toward the middle of the screen when the bubble sits near an edge
ElevenLabs Scribe turns your speech into text as you talk; Claude can then tidy it up. Your audio and text go to those services under your own API keys, which are stored encrypted on this phone.
Allow the microphone in Bubble Keyboard settings
Needs speech-to-text access. Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys.
Removes filler words, fixes punctuation and applies spoken corrections (\"Tuesday, no, Wednesday\"). Adds a short pause after you let go. Create a key at console.anthropic.com.
The fastest model works best here.
Paste a new key to replace the saved one
Couldn\'t store the key securely on this phone
Words appear in the text field as you talk, and the polished version replaces them when it\'s ready. Off: words preview above the bubble and are typed when you finish. Password fields always preview.

Dictated messages never end with a period, because a final period reads as cold. Question marks, exclamation marks and periods between sentences stay. Keep talking after a message and its period comes back before the new words.

Dictation finishes by itself after this long without a recognized word (background noise doesn\'t count). Halfway there (at most 5 seconds in) what you\'ve said so far is cleaned up while it keeps listening; keep talking and the next cleanup sees both, so corrections still work.
A text box to practice in
Add an ElevenLabs key to start
Two quick steps and the bubble shows up whenever you type.
Tap the bubble to open the ring; press and hold it to talk.
No countdown: it stays open until you fold it. You can also pull the up arrow out to its pin.
Faint icons just outside the open ring, beyond each key, for what holding it does. The keys themselves stay clean.
Up: pin the ring open, or unpin it
A pin on the center shows it\'s pinned
Hold an arrow until its icon appears beyond it, then slide out onto the icon and let go.

Four keys, the same as the bubble\'s notches: up opens the full keyboard, right the cursor joystick, down settings, and left pastes (grayed out when the clipboard has nothing to paste). Tap the center to dictate. While you dictate, the left key is a red ✕ that throws it away.
The ring has the same four keys as the bubble\'s notches: keyboard, joystick, settings, and paste.
Slide up to the joystick and let go
Drag to move · hold still, then drag to select
Selecting · keep a finger down, drag with another to go further
A one-row bar under the app
A bubble over the app, with notches and a ring
no list price known for that model, so its tokens are counted but not priced

Estimated from what this phone sent, at list prices: Scribe v2 Realtime at $%1$.2f per hour of audio, and %2$s at %3$s. Plan allowances, free hours and credits aren\'t taken into account, so your actual bill can be lower; the ElevenLabs and Claude Console dashboards have the real numbers. Only counts are kept here, never your words or audio.
Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys, with speech-to-text access, and paste it here.
Create one at console.anthropic.com under API keys and paste it here.

Tap it and the ring opens already listening. Or press it and four notches appear: slide left to paste, right for the cursor joystick, up for the full keyboard, down for settings, and let go once it clicks in. Hold as long as you like: the notches stay up, and letting go without choosing one does nothing. To move the bubble, slide diagonally, or keep going past a notch and it breaks free.
Tap the bubble and the ring opens already listening. Keep talking. Tap the center when you\'re done, or the red ✕ on the left to throw it away. It also finishes by itself after a stretch of silence.
Tap to move the cursor. Tap, then tap and hold an arrow to repeat it. Backspace repeats on a plain hold.
Hold an arrow on the ring and its socket appears beyond it; pull the key out into it and let go. Up pins the ring, right opens the cursor joystick, down opens settings, left folds the ring.
Tap abc for the full keyboard; slide along its space bar to move the cursor, and tap abc (now a ✕) to fold it away. Hold space for punctuation or enter for numbers, slide to a key and let go.
Select text and cut, copy, paste and delete appear beside the bubble. To paste anytime, slide left from the bubble or tap the ring\'s left key.

Slide right from the bubble (or pull the ring\'s right arrow out). Push the knob to aim (a highlighted letter marks the spot), tap the knob to put the cursor there, or hold it still for a click and then push to select. The ✕ on the rim folds it away. The keyboard button below the ✕ goes straight to the full keyboard; from the keyboard, hold the comma and slide up onto Joystick to come back.
Slide the bubble diagonally (or drag on past a notch) to move it anywhere; each orientation remembers its spot. Flick it diagonally and it glides out of the way.
Tap the bubble to talk, or press it and slide to a notch.
Cursor joystick: push the knob to aim, tap it to move the cursor there, hold then push to select. The close button is on the rim.
Cursor, keyboard and voice in the middle. Hold delete for space and return.
Space and return on the bar. Hold delete to keep deleting.
ABC switches to Gboard instead of opening the built-in keyboard. A button on Gboard brings the voice bar back.
Off. Tap to turn on Bubble Keyboard in Accessibility settings (if Android says it\'s restricted, allow restricted settings in the app\'s App info first).
Gboard isn\'t turned on as a keyboard. Tap to open keyboard settings.
Turn on Gboard in Android\'s keyboard settings first
Bubble Keyboard: way back from Gboard

While Gboard is open, shows a bar on top of it, a mic in its voice-key spot, or a floating mic bubble; tap it to switch back to Bubble Keyboard\'s voice bar. It reads only Gboard\'s window: where it is, where its keys are (to find the voice key) and its background color. It doesn\'t read the app you\'re typing in or what you type.
A strip in Gboard\'s own color, joined to its top edge, that says Tap to return
A mic where Gboard\'s voice key is. Covers Gboard\'s mic, or, if you turn Gboard\'s voice key off (Gboard ▸ Voice typing), sits at the right end of Gboard\'s top row, toolbar or suggestions.
A mic bubble above Gboard; drag it anywhere
